- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, especially if recent price is trending up.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward moves in history; apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 1–3% for the next 3–5 days post-spike.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after peak or rises after trough), model often fails to adjust; apply a lagged correction: if 3–5 days ago was a peak, reduce forecast by 2–5%.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: if sentiment >0.67, apply 10–20% dampening; if sentiment <0.33, apply 10–20% amplification.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.67” or “1.00” with no price movement, model may overfit; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid false momentum.
